summary: Added PtyLiveSessions, the adapter that owns terminals: open() spawns <shell> -il through the injected TerminalSpawn, names the session after the basename of the shell, and remembers it; onData appends to a per-session scrollback trimmed to the last 262144 characters and fans bytes out to every live watcher; onExit forgets the session so find/all stop naming it; watch() answers the scrollback plus a stop() that removes only that watcher; the environment forces TERM and drops undefined entries. Driven entirely with a doubled TerminalSpawn/Terminal in the test — no node-pty dependency and no ct-api.ts wiring, both left for task 3 as the brief scopes them. TDD: watched 'a watcher receives what the terminal printed before it arrived' fail red (printed was '' instead of 'hello world') before restoring the scrollback-join line, then green. All 9 named Tests: cases are present and pass. Ran a manual mutation sweep on every production line that isn't the constructor: the off-by-one on the scrollback slice, the environment's undefined-filter, watch's stop(), onExit's forget, the SHELL-unset fallback and the basename computation were each mutated by hand and each broke a test — except one real gap the sweep caught: the two toEqual assertions on the recorded spawn options (env in particular) initially survived a mutation that stopped dropping undefined entries, because toEqual treats an explicit undefined property as equal to a missing key. Fixed both to toStrictEqual and added an explicit Object.keys(...).not.toContain('GHOST') check, then re-ran the mutation to confirm it now fails. One line is intentionally undefended by a test: #terminalFor's throw for a LiveSession this instance never opened — the brief's Tests: list has no case for it and every call this task exercises always passes a session this same instance just opened, so per testing.md it is the guard defending an invariant the current call graph cannot violate, not a missing test; it stays because P-1 (headers written between find() and watch()) means a future caller could race it, and it is not this task's job to add that caller. Verification: npm run typecheck exit 0; npm test -- __tests__/infrastructure/pty-live-sessions.test.ts exit 0 (9 passed); npm test exit 0 (63 files, 1526 tests passed, no existing suite broke).

The stream that reaches the page while the process runs
summary: WatchLiveSession is a thin application query that hands its params straight to LiveSessions.watch() and wraps the port's {printed, stop} answer in its own frozen WatchLiveSessionResult. SessionStreamRoute finds the session, refuses null with a 400 session-not-live, otherwise writes SSE headers, subscribes through WatchLiveSession with an onBytes that writes each later frame, registers request.on('close') to call stop() and end() and nothing else, then writes one frame with the printed scrollback the subscription answered -- closing the page never reaches the port with anything but stop(). Deviated from the brief's literal wording once and I'm flagging it: the brief said ApiServer 'gains a watchLiveSession collaborator' (singular), implying SessionStreamRoute.handledBy's first argument (liveSessions: LiveSessions) could be reached via this.listLiveSessions!.liveSessions. I tried that first and it broke server.start() for every other route's test suite that omits listLiveSessions (6 files, 163 tests), because #route() would then dereference .liveSessions on undefined eagerly at mount time, unlike every other collaborator in that method which is only captured in a closure and touched at request time. I added a real liveSessions?: LiveSessions|null collaborator field to ApiServer instead (same optional/nullable/lazy pattern as its siblings), which keeps mounting side-effect-free and is why the diff has two new ApiServer fields instead of one. ct-api.ts (the composition root) is outside this task's Files line and was left untouched, so the two new collaborators aren't wired into the real running backend yet -- that wiring belongs to whichever later task turns this on end to end. Also cast request.params[ID_PARAMETER] as string once (Express types params as string|string[] in general, but a non-repeating :id segment is always a string for this exact route); adding a typeof guard instead would be an unreachable branch this repo's own testing.md would flag as 'the line nobody needs' since no real request can hit the array case here, so I kept the cast, consistent with the same pattern already used in git-workspace.ts and start-plan-route.ts. TDD: watch-live-session.test.ts and session-stream-route.test.ts's first test were both red for the right reason (missing module) before any production code existed. I additionally hand-broke and restored three lines to confirm the tests actually catch regressions: dropping watched.stop() from the close handler and muting the onBytes wiring both now fail fast (2s, via a WithinBudget test helper) with a message naming what didn't happen, instead of hanging on this repo's 120s global testTimeout as they did on my first pass -- I hardened the test's frame/stop waits with that budget once I saw the hang. Verification: npm --prefix backend run typecheck (exit 0), npm --prefix backend test -- __tests__/infrastructure/session-stream-route.test.ts (exit 0, 5/5), npm --prefix backend test -- __tests__/application/watch-live-session.test.ts (exit 0, 1/1), npm --prefix backend test (exit 0, 66 files / 1551 tests).
